ant-min-mount-ruker-bif.st: Largest known iron formation in Antarctica; not economic
ant-min-mount-ruker-bif.dt: Soviet (Ravich and others) and Australian (Tingey) geological studies, as reviewed by USGS in 1983
ant-min-mount-ruker-bif.what: USGS Circular 909: the largest known iron-formation deposits in Antarctica are at Mount Ruker, beds up to 70 m thick in a main sequence about 400 m thick, total iron 25-46% (average 34%), phosphorus too high for good steel ore; aeromagnetic anomalies extend west for 120 km under the ice (Soviet work by Ravich and others, 1982; Australian work by Tingey).

ant-min-newman-nunataks-bif.n: Newman Nunataks banded iron formation, Enderby Land
ant-min-newman-nunataks-bif.what: USGS Circular 909: 'In 1977, Australian geologists reported the discovery of the largest deposit of banded iron-formation in Enderby Land, at Newman Nunataks'; 750 m long, 150 m wide, 20 m thick, average 34% iron.

ant-min-beacon-coal.n: Permian-Triassic coal of the Beacon Supergroup (Transantarctic Mountains; Beaver Lake, Prince Charles Mountains)
ant-min-beacon-coal.dt: Known since early expeditions; reviewed by USGS 1974 and 1983
ant-min-beacon-coal.what: USGS Circular 909: coal is widespread in Permian-Triassic rocks, with thick beds in the Beacon Supergroup of the Transantarctic Mountains and at Beaver Lake; 'None of the deposits are economically recoverable'.
fig: Known since early expeditions; reviewed by USGS 1974 and 1983

ant-min-offshore-basins.n: Offshore sedimentary basins (Ross, Weddell, Bellingshausen and others): petroleum potential
ant-min-offshore-basins.st: No known petroleum resources; no drilling for petroleum
ant-min-offshore-basins.dt: Multichannel seismic surveys by several countries from 1976; DSDP holes in the Ross Sea, 1973
ant-min-offshore-basins.what: USGS Circular 909 (Behrendt): 'No known petroleum resources occur in Antarctica'; thick sedimentary basins have been found by seismic surveys, but there has been no offshore drilling beneath the shelf since the 1973 DSDP holes.

ant-min-russia-weddell-surveys.n: Russian geological and seismic surveys, Weddell Sea and British Antarctic Territory sector (Rosgeo)
ant-min-russia-weddell-surveys.st: Surveys continue; UK government says no evidence of drilling or extraction
ant-min-russia-weddell-surveys.dt: Long-running; raised in UK Parliament, May 2024
ant-min-russia-weddell-surveys.what: UK FCDO written answer HL4614 (24 May 2024): Russia has a long-standing programme of surveying and mapping Antarctic geology and has assured the ATCM it is for science; 'There is no evidence of any drilling or extraction activities.' A widely reported figure of 511 billion barrels was presented to the Commons Environmental Audit Committee but is not confirmed in any official government source, so it is not stored.
